title: Guess the Feeling
goal: Children look at their teacher's face and body, notice which feeling it shows, and learn that friends' faces show feelings too.

steps.title: Hello
steps.heading: Feelings show on our faces!
steps.cue: Gather the children so they can see the TV. Wave along when the character says hello, and give a big smile on the last line.
lines: Feelings peek out on our faces.
Today we'll look closely at your teacher's face.

steps.title: Which feeling is it?
steps.cue: Pick one feeling card and make that face, big and clear. When the children raise their hands, count each feeling and tap +. Once everyone is counted, tap Confirm. Try another card if you like.
steps.prompt: Look at your teacher's face. Which feeling is it?
lines: Look closely at your teacher's face.
Which feeling is it right now?
Raise your hand for the feeling you see!

options.label: Happy
options.hint: corners of the mouth up, eyes like half-moons

steps.on_confirm: You noticed {guess_list}. [[guess_lead: Most of you saw {guess_lead}.]] [[sad: Thank you for noticing a sad face.]] [[angry: An angry face is a feeling too. Thank you for noticing it.]] [[scared: Thank you for noticing a scared feeling.]] When we look closely, faces show us feelings.

steps.title: Copy the face
steps.heading: Let's make feelings with our faces!
steps.cue: Start the timer and call out one feeling at a time. The children copy it with their faces and bodies. When 45 seconds are up, the character wraps it up.
lines: Now let's make feelings with our faces!
When your teacher says a feeling,

moves.text: Happy: corners of your mouth up, eyes like half-moons
Sad: eyebrows down, let your mouth droop
Angry: pull your eyebrows together and cross your arms
Scared: big eyes, shoulders up to your ears

steps.done_line: Wow, every feeling showed up on our faces! Now let's sit back down.

steps.title: Our class story today
steps.heading: The feelings our class noticed
steps.cue: The character reads a story made from today's numbers. Afterwards, ask: 'What could we do when a friend has a sad face?'
steps.template: Today {class} looked closely at a teacher's face. We thought about the feeling and raised our hands. Here is what we noticed: {guess_list}. [[guess_lead: Most friends saw {guess_lead}.]] Our friends' faces show feelings too: happy, sad, angry and scared. When we look closely and ask 'Are you okay?', a friend's heart feels a little warmer.

steps.title: Our Class Book
steps.cue: The TV turns into a picture book of the feelings our class noticed today and reads it page by page. When it's done, tap Next.
steps.cover_line: Here is a book of the feelings our class noticed today.

steps.title: Goodbye
steps.heading: Thank you for today!
steps.cue: When the character finishes saying goodbye, tap Finish lesson. The family page link will be ready.
lines: Thank you for noticing my feelings today.
At home, look closely at your family's faces too.

outro: That's all for today! Thank you for looking so closely.

home.title: Keep it going at home
tips: Make a face and ask, 'Look at me. Which feeling is this?' When your child names one, answer with 'That's how it looked to you.'
While reading a picture book, ask now and then, 'How is this character feeling?' Looking at the face and the body together makes it easier.
When your child shows a sad or angry face, say what you see first: 'You look sad.' Often, being noticed is enough.
home.note: This page shows only class totals and the class story. No individual child's choice is recorded.
